t: From Copernicus in 1543 to Newton in 1687, European scholars replaced the Earth-centred cosmos and Aristotle’s physics with a Sun-centred system governed by mathematical laws.
Its people joined mathematics, measurement and experiment, used new instruments such as the telescope, microscope and air pump, and shared their results in books, letters, journals and academies.
Historians debate how revolutionary it was: it built on Greek, Islamic and medieval learning, and the name itself became common only in the 20th century.
dyk: Newton’s Principia was printed in 1687 at the expense of Edmond Halley, partly because the Royal Society had spent its funds on an expensive illustrated History of Fishes by Francis Willughby and John Ray.
ev: Nicolaus Copernicus publishes On the Revolutions; Andreas Vesalius publishes On the Fabric of the Human Body
Tycho Brahe observes a new star and shows that it lies beyond the Moon, in heavens thought unchangeable
Johannes Kepler’s New Astronomy shows that Mars moves in an ellipse around the Sun
Galileo’s Starry Messenger reports mountains on the Moon and four moons of Jupiter
William Harvey shows that the blood circulates, pumped by the heart
The Roman Inquisition condemns Galileo for defending the motion of the Earth
The Royal Society is founded in London
Isaac Newton publishes the Principia, with the laws of motion and universal gravitation

f.where: Universities, courts and cities across Europe, from Poland, Italy, Denmark and Bohemia to the German lands, England, France and the Dutch Republic, linked by printed books, letters and, later, scientific societies
f.period: 1543–1687 by a common convention, from Copernicus’s On the Revolutions to Newton’s Principia; often taken more broadly as c. 1500–1700
f.figures: Nicolaus Copernicus, Johannes Kepler, Galileo Galilei, René Descartes, Robert Boyle, Isaac Newton
f.outcome: A Sun-centred cosmos governed by universal mathematical laws, the experimental method, and lasting scientific institutions such as the Royal Society and the Académie des sciences
